title: Protocol for analysis of senescent neuronal stem cells in genetic-modified embryonic mice using in utero electroporation technique
protocol: Pre-heat normal saline to 38°C.
Prepare cesarean section operating table.
Sterilize surgical instruments necessary for cesarean section surgery by heat sterilization.
Adjust and ensure the voltage, time, and frequency of electroporation.
Mix plasmids with Fast Green (0.1 mg/mL) at a ratio of 99:1 (v/v).
Sterilize surgery tools with 75% ethanol.
Sterilize the operation area with 75% ethanol.
Sterilize electrodes with 75% ethanol.
Anesthetize pregnant Rack1F/F mouse by injecting 1% sodium pentobarbital (6 mg/kg).
Prepare anesthetic immediately before use.
Choose alternative legal anesthetics if necessary.
Anesthetize each pregnant mouse one at a time.
Place the anesthetized mouse gently on the operation table.
Fix the limbs of the mouse with adhesive tape.
Remove hair from the abdomen using depilatory cream.
Cover the body of the mouse with sterile gauze, except for the abdomen and head.
Disinfect the abdomen of the mouse with betadine.
Lift skin at the middle of the lower abdomen with tweezers.
Make an incision about 1 cm in length with ophthalmic scissors.
Keep the incision moist with warm (about 37°C) sterile saline.
Gently pull out the uterine horn to expose embryos.
Inject each embryo's lateral ventricle with 1 μg of plasmid DNA mixed with 1% Fast Green for a total volume of 1 μL using a glass pulled micropipette.
Electroporate expression constructs using an ECM 830 electroporator with five 50 ms pulses separated by 950 ms intervals at 40 V.
Inject plasmids into five different embryos in at least three independent operations.
Reposition uterine horns carefully into the abdominal cavity after electroporation.
Bathe the abdominal cavity with pre-warmed sterile saline.
Suture the wound closed after bathing.
Place mice on a heating pad until recovery from anesthesia.
Monitor mice for pain carefully post-recovery and return them to their home cage.
Prepare pregnant mice at E18.5 by euthanizing them with intraperitoneal sodium pentobarbital injection approved by the animal welfare committee.
Collect brains from electroporated embryos at E18.5 for dissociation, fixation, dehydration, and frozen sectioning.
Put the anesthetized pregnant mouse slightly on the operation table.
Dissect the abdomen of the anesthetized pregnant mouse with fine scissors.
Take out all the embryos from the pregnant mouse under a binocular microscope and place them in 37°C normal saline.
Dissect the brains under a binocular microscope using fine microsurgical tweezers.
Collect each brain into a 4% paraformaldehyde solution in a 10 mL centrifuge tube.
Remove the meninges from the surface of the brain carefully with fine microsurgical tweezers.
Fix the brains in paraformaldehyde for 24 hours.
Dehydrate the tissues first with 15% sucrose for 24 hours and then with 30% sucrose for 48 hours.
Place the tissues in a 1:1 solution of 30% sucrose/OCT for 1–2 hours at 4°C.
Place the tissues in 100% OCT compound for 1 hour at 4°C.
Embed the tissues in 100% OCT compound and freeze them in Cryomold at -20°C.
Take the slices out from freezer and warm them up to room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 10 min.
Fix brain sections in fixative for 15 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash the slices three times with PBS for 5 min each.

Prepare the SA-β-Gal solution by mixing each 1 mL of staining solution with 10 μL of potassium ferrocyanide, 10 μL of potassium ferricyanide, 100 μL of X-Gal, and 880 μL of citric acid-sodium phosphate buffer.
Stain the slices immediately with SA-β-Gal staining solution (pH 6.0) for 24 h in the incubator at 37°C protected from light.
Rinse the slices with PBS for three times after the blue color is developed.
Wash the slices with PBS.
Permeabilize the slices with 1% PBST for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Block the slices with 3% BSA in 0.3% PBST for 1 hour at room temperature.
Incubate the brain samples on the slide with anti-GFP (1:500) and anti-Sox2 (1:400) primary antibodies overnight at 4°C.
Wash the sections three times with PBS, each wash lasting 5 minutes.
Incubate the sections with Alexa Fluor 568- or Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibodies for 3 hours at room temperature.
Wash the sections five times with PBS, each wash lasting 5 minutes.
Mount the slices with medium containing DAPI.
Use confocal microscope to obtain the fluorescence imaging picture.
Make a special symbol on the slide to distinguish each sample.
Use digital slide scanner with a 20× objective to acquire brightfield photomicrographs of SA-β-Gal staining.
